body:
# Simple Home Manager Solution

If you're not using VSCodium, update the `basePath`. Also make sure you disable auto update in the extensions list.
Note: If you're on arm, you might have to change linux-x64.

This goes in your home manager file.
```nix
{ inputs, pkgs, lib, ... }:

let
  # Update this to .vscode or whatever your extensions parent folder is
  basePath = ".vscode-oss";

  # Reference to the extension from nixpkgs
  continuePkg = pkgs.vscode-extensions.continue.continue;

  # Construct the specific folder name VSCodium expects: publisher.name-version-platform
  # Note: The 'linux-x64' suffix is required for extensions with binaries like Continue
  continueDirName = lib.toLower "${continuePkg.vscodeExtPublisher}.${continuePkg.vscodeExtName}-${continuePkg.version}-linux-x64";
in
{
  programs.vscode = {
    enable = true;
    package = pkgs.vscodium;
    # Leave 'extensions' empty here to keep the directory mutable
  };

  # Symlink it
  home.file."${basePath}/extensions/${continueDirName}" = {
    source = "${pkgs.vscode-extensions.continue.continue}/share/vscode/extensions/${continuePkg.vscodeExtPublisher}.${continuePkg.vscodeExtName}";
  };
}
```

# Example Config

I added some example models I have installed and they all work.

```nix
  home.file.".continue/config.yaml".text = ''
    name: "Nix Local Config"
    version: "1.0.0"
    schema: "v1"

    models:
      - name: "qwen3-coder"
        title: "Qwen 3 Coder (Local)"
        provider: "ollama"
        model: "qwen3-coder:latest"
        apiBase: "http://localhost:11434"
        roles: ["chat", "edit", "apply"]

      - name: "gemma3"
        title: "Gemma 3 27B"
        provider: "ollama"
        model: "gemma3:27b"
        apiBase: "http://localhost:11434"
        roles: ["chat"]

      - name: "gpt-oss"
        title: "GPT-OSS 120B"
        provider: "ollama"
        model: "gpt-oss:120b"
        apiBase: "http://localhost:11434"
        roles: ["chat"]

      - name: "llama-autocomplete"
        title: "Llama 3.2 1B Autocomplete"
        provider: "ollama"
        model: "llama3.2:1b"
        apiBase: "http://localhost:11434"
        roles: ["autocomplete", "embed"]

    slashCommands:
      - name: "edit"
        description: "Edit selected code"
      - name: "comment"
        description: "Add comments to code"
      - name: "cmd"
        description: "Generate shell command"

    # This prevents Continue from appending or searching for other models
    allowAnonymousTelemetry: false

    # Map the specific roles to your models
    ui:
      codeBlockRenderMode: "preview"
  '';
  home.file.".continue/config.json".text = ""; # Avoid adding a value here, you might end up with a double json object bug.
```

Just a little FYI for anyone in a similar situation, and using nginx or nginx-proxy-manager:

As the Ollama.ts code seems to use as `apiKey` option, but sets it as `Bearer` Auth-Token i just added a little custom snippet in my nginx-proxy-manager config to handle the authentication, instead of the regular (Basic) Auth config, that does not work:

continue config.json
```
"apiBase": "https://ollama....",
"apiKey": "THETOKEN"
```

nginx-proxy manager advanced host config:
```
set $auth_header $http_authorization;
if ($auth_header !~* "^Bearer THETOKEN$") {
        return 403;
}
```

body:
Looks to be an issue when building sqlite3 and onnxruntime-node, Same issue occurs for me on Apple silicon, Solution for me was to run the following ( the same approach should also work on W11 ARM as well )...
```shell
# change to plugin directory
cd ~/.vscode/extensions/continue.continue-*

# remove sqlite3 and onnxruntime libraries
npm uninstall sqlite3 onnxruntime-node

# reinstall with targetet architecture flags 
npm install sqlite3 onnxruntime-node --build-from-source --target_arch=arm64 --fallback-to-build

# copy onnxruntime binaries to output folders
cp ./node_modules/libonnxruntime.1.17.3.dylib ./bin/napi-v3/darwin/arm64/libonnxruntime.1.17.3.dylib
cp ./node_modules/onnxruntime_binding.node ./bin/napi-v3/darwin/arm64/onnxruntime_binding.node

# copy sqlite binary to build output folder
cp ./node_modules/sqlite3/build/Release/node_sqlite3.node ./out/build/Release/node_sqlite3.node
```

body:
I created a script that simplifies the update with the files provided by @svantesorberg .
Just download the bundles.zip and place it into the same directory as this script. 
Running this script should update the relevant files of the current continue extension so the extension should work on Windows on ARM64. 


```python
import os
import shutil
import zipfile

def get_extension_directory(username):
    base_path = f"C:\\Users\\{username}\\.vscode\\extensions"
    all_dirs = [d for d in os.listdir(base_path) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(base_path, d))]
    
    matching_dirs = [d for d in all_dirs if d.startswith("continue.continue-") and "win32-arm64" in d]
    
    if len(matching_dirs) == 0:
        print(f"No directories found matching the criteria.")
        raise Exception("Could not find any matching extension directory.")
    elif len(matching_dirs) > 1:
        print(f"Found multiple directories matching the criteria: {matching_dirs}")
        raise Exception("Found more than one matching extension directory.")
    
    return os.path.join(base_path, matching_dirs[0])

def unpack_bundle(zip_path, extract_to):
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as zip_ref:
        zip_ref.extractall(extract_to)

def main():
    # Get the current user's username
    try:
        username = os.getlogin()
    except OSError:
        print("Could not determine the current user. Using environment variable USERPROFILE.")
        username = os.path.basename(os.environ['USERPROFILE'])
    
    print(f"Using username: {username}")
    
    # Locate the VS Code extension directory
    try:
        extension_dir = get_extension_directory(username)
        print(f"Found extension directory: {extension_dir}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(e)
        return
    
    # Define paths for unpacking and copying
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    bundle_zip_path = os.path.join(script_dir, "bundles.zip")  # Renamed to bundles.zip
    temp_extract_dir = os.path.join(script_dir, "temp_extract")
    
    if not os.path.exists(bundle_zip_path):
        raise Exception("bundles.zip not found in the script directory.")
    
    # Unpack bundles.zip
    unpack_bundle(bundle_zip_path, temp_extract_dir)
    print(f"Unpacked {bundle_zip_path} to {temp_extract_dir}")
    
    # Define source and destination paths for copying files
    node_sqlite3_source = os.path.join(temp_extract_dir, "node_sqlite3.node")
    vectordb_source = os.path.join(temp_extract_dir, "vectordb-win32-arm64-msvc")
    
    out_build_release_dest = os.path.join(extension_dir, "out", "build", "Release")
    node_modules_lancedb_dest = os.path.join(extension_dir, "out", "node_modules", "@lancedb", "vectordb-win32-arm64-msvc")  # Ensure the directory is copied as a whole
    
    # Ensure destination directories exist
    os.makedirs(out_build_release_dest, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(node_modules_lancedb_dest), exist_ok=True)  # Create parent directories if they don't exist
    
    # Copy files and directories
    shutil.copy2(node_sqlite3_source, out_build_release_dest)
    print(f"Copied {node_sqlite3_source} to {out_build_release_dest}")
    
    shutil.rmtree(node_modules_lancedb_dest, ignore_errors=True)  # Remove existing directory if it exists
    shutil.copytree(vectordb_source, node_modules_lancedb_dest)
    print(f"Copied {vectordb_source} to {node_modules_lancedb_dest}")
    
    # Clean up temporary extraction directory
    shutil.rmtree(temp_extract_dir)
    print(f"Cleaned up temporary extraction directory: {temp_extract_dir}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

body:
A bit more detailed description to the above (of @aoliva71):
1. Clone lancedb: `git clone https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb`
2. Modify the config.toml: `vi lancedb/.cargo/config.toml`
3. Delete the [target] sections, except for the [target.'cfg(all())'] and add a new one with the following content:
`[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
rustflags = ["-C", "target-cpu=x86-64", "-C", "target-feature=+avx"]`
4. Save it, then jump to lancedb/nodejs: `cd lancedb/nodejs`.
5. I highly recommend removing unnecessary build options from `package.json` by looking through the json, removing the "napi.triples.additional" values except for "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"; removing unwanted cpu architectures from "cpu" and removing unwanted os from "os".
6. Run `npm run build`. This produces the dist/lancedb.linux-x64-gnu.node above.
7. (leave this folder `cd ../../` and) Clone continue: `git clone https://github.com/continuedev/continue.git`
8. Don't mess around with anything like testing, just build according to: https://github.com/continuedev/continue.git (nvm use to test version and use it, cd to continue/extensions/vscode, then npm run package).
9. (leave folder by `cd ../../../` and) Unzip the .vsix `mkdir tmp_vsix && unzip continue/extensions/vscode/build/continue-{VERSION}.vsix -d tmp_vsix`
10. Replace the index.node: `cp lancedb/nodejs/dist/lancedb.linux-x64-gnu.node tmp_vsix/extension/out/node_modules/@lancedb/vectordb-linux-x64-gnu/index.node`
11. Zip back the vsix: `cd tmp_vsix && zip -r fixed-continue.vsix * && mv fixed-continue.vsix ../ && cd ../`
12. Install in VSCode by opening Extensions, clicking the three dots near the refresh button above, then Install from VSIX... and browse the file we created earlier.

Enjoy.

PS.: Sorry for the possibly too detailed description, some of us are not devs with CI/CD and/or build experience, however we still want to solve the issue. This comment is a detailed help for such people.
If the instructions are unclear, or incorrect, please let me know so I can edit the comment and correct possible mistakes.
